goals: Mechanistic: quantify how water partitioning (ET / surface runoff / drainage-recharge) varies with elevation across the Bow River headwaters
Validation: compare partitioning / streamflow against in-domain observations
key_processes: snowmelt-driven runoff vs recharge vs ET partitioning

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM can produce water partitioning at points, but the elevation mechanism requires elevation-resolved forcing that is unavailable outside CONUS.

answerable: Soil-texture control on partitioning at a representative site under a single forcing (a DIFFERENT, secondary question — not elevation-resolved)

not_answerable.why: Domain is in Canada; NLDAS (the only elevation-resolved forcing) is CONUS-only, so forcing falls back to Qian T62 ~1.9°, which delivers ~one uniform climate over this basin. Elevation cannot drive precip/temperature, so an elevation-stratified column set would reflect soil, not elevation.
not_answerable.needs: Elevation-resolved forcing for Canada (NLDAS-equivalent Canadian product, e.g. RDRS/ERA5-downscaled)

not_answerable.aspect: Elevation-driven snow accumulation/melt gradient controlling partitioning
not_answerable.why: Without elevation-resolved forcing, precip phase and temperature are uniform across columns, so no snowpack gradient forms across the rain-snow transition.
not_answerable.needs: Elevation-downscaled forcing (precip/temperature lapse) for the Canadian domain

not_answerable.why: Only ECCC gauges exist in-domain and they are not ingested by the stack; SNOTEL is US-only. Gauge comparison also needs routing/aggregation the single-column stack lacks.
not_answerable.needs: ECCC gauge + Canadian snow-obs ingest, and runoff routing/aggregation

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (CONDITIONAL — valid only once Canadian elevation-resolved forcing exists; presented as the design to run then, not now)

classes: dominant SSURGO-equivalent texture per band (from Canadian soil raster, TBD)

sampling_strategy.n_justification: 4 elevation bands spanning the 2200 m relief and the rain-snow transition, x ~1 dominant soil per band, with light replication (~3 per band) to separate soil variance from the elevation signal. Kept small because the design is exploratory and cannot yet run.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate in the montane/subalpine rain-snow transition band (1800-2900 m) where snowpack, melt timing, and the runoff/recharge/ET split are most sensitive; oversample valley bottoms where drainage/recharge dominates.
sampling_strategy.replication: ~3 columns per elevation band to sample within-band soil heterogeneity and separate it from the elevation trend.

sampling_plan.reason: Baseline low-elevation partitioning; drainage/recharge-dominated end member (CONDITIONAL on Canadian forcing).
Most sensitive band where snow-vs-rain partitioning governs the ET/runoff/recharge split (CONDITIONAL on Canadian forcing).
Snow-dominated accumulation zone controlling melt-driven runoff timing (CONDITIONAL on Canadian forcing).
High-elevation end member; thin soils, snow-dominated, low ET (CONDITIONAL on Canadian forcing).

validation_design.comparison: aggregated — would require summing/routing column runoff to a gauge point
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — ECCC gauges not in stack

validation_design.comparison: none — SNOTEL is US-only; no in-domain snow obs ingested

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: CONDITIONAL Canadian elevation-resolved forcing, native soil per column — NOT runnable on the current stack

requires_capabilities.capability: Elevation-resolved forcing for Canada (NLDAS-equivalent, e.g. RDRS or downscaled ERA5)
requires_capabilities.why: NLDAS is CONUS-only; the question is entirely about elevation acting through precip/snow, which Qian T62 (~1.9°) cannot resolve
Only in-domain hydrologic observation, currently not in stack

requires_capabilities.capability: Canadian snow observation ingest (e.g. ECCC/BC snow pillows)
requires_capabilities.why: SNOTEL is US-only; snow is the dominant partitioning control here

requires_capabilities.capability: Runoff routing / aggregation to gauge points
requires_capabilities.why: Single-column ELM has no lateral transport; gauge comparison needs aggregation

requires_capabilities.capability: Spin-up / WTD-informed warm start for the Canadian domain
requires_capabilities.why: Recharge/water-table targets require it, and Fan (2013) warm start is set up for CONUS points

assumptions: Bow River headwaters lie outside NLDAS coverage, so the stack would default to non-elevation-resolved Qian T62 forcing.
No in-domain observations are ingestible by the current stack (ECCC not wired in, SNOTEL US-only).
Elevation bands are illustrative; a downstream expander would set concrete points from a Canadian DEM once forcing is available.
open_questions: Is a Canadian elevation-resolved forcing product (RDRS, ERA5-Land, WFDE5) acceptable as an NLDAS substitute, and can it be ingested?
Can ECCC hydrometric and snow-course data be added to the observation ingest?
If elevation-resolved forcing cannot be provided, does the user want the fallback soil-sensitivity experiment (explicitly NOT elevation-resolved) instead?
